data.goal: Assess RNA-protein agreement for cardiomyocytes, hepatocytes and neutrophils in the Human Protein Atlas using single-cell-type RNA nCPM and Deep Visual Proteomics cell-type Intensity. Join by Ensembl ID and those exact cell-type names. For each cell type separately retain genes with positive measurements in both modalities, report the retained count, Spearman correlation and overlap/Jaccard of the top twenty genes ranked independently by RNA and by protein. Give the top-twenty lists with values.…

data.text:
Looking at the current state, I have the retained gene sets, top-20 lists, and Spearman correlations. Now I need to:
1. Compute percentiles and identify top-5 discordant genes per cell type
2. Compute top-20 overlap (intersection) per cell type
3. Build scatter plot data (union of top-20 lists)

These are all independent chains, so I'll run them together.

limitations: Spearman correlation measures rank concordance across all retained genes; it does not capture whether absolute expression levels agree or whether the relationship is linear on any scale.
DVP cell-type Intensity is a deconvolved estimate from tissue-level imaging, not a direct single-cell measurement; its resolution and dynamic range differ fundamentally from scRNA-seq nCPM.
The top-20 overlap and Jaccard metrics are sensitive to the arbitrary cutoff of 20; a different list size would yield different overlap values.

Histone variant genes (H4C1–H4C15) appear as separate Ensembl entries with near-identical RNA nCPM values (all tied at the same rank), which inflates their representation in the discordant-gene list; they may represent a single biological signal split across paralog entries.
Subcellular location annotations are available for only 6 of the 14 unique discordant genes; the remaining 8 have no annotation in the HPA subcellular location table.
The analysis uses the HPA master table as the gene universe; genes absent from this table (e.g., some pseudogenes or recently annotated loci) are excluded.
